einzeiler: Alex Morris on distilling three decades of Berkshire Hathaway meetings into a book.
kurzfassung: Alex Morris discusses his book "Buffett and Munger Unscripted," which distills three decades of Berkshire Hathaway annual meetings. He shares insights on his concentrated investment strategy, the evolution of value investing, and lessons learned from studying Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger. Additionally, Morris reflects on his transition from a buy-side analyst to launching an independent research service.
stichpunkte: Alex Morris is the author of "Buffett and Munger Unscripted" and founder of TSOH Investment Research Service.
He analyzed three decades of Berkshire Hathaway shareholder meetings, distilling thousands of questions into a comprehensive book.
Morris follows a concentrated portfolio strategy, typically holding ten to fifteen names.
He highlights the importance of temperament, emotional stability, and independent thinking in investing.
The conversation covers major market shifts, including Buffett's transition into tech and Apple.
Morris discusses the significance of the Berkshire Hathaway leadership transition to Greg Abel.
He emphasizes continuous learning, writing as a tool for clear thinking, and expanding one's circle of competence.
